title: Salade niçoise
summary: A Provençal salad of tuna, eggs, tomatoes, olives and green beans dressed with sharp Dijon vinaigrette.
ingredients: 2 x 125 g cans tuna in olive oil, drained
method: Boil the eggs in a saucepan over high heat, then medium-high, for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm. Cool in iced water, then peel and quarter.
Blanch the green beans in salted boiling water over high heat for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Cool in cold water, then drain and dry.
Whisk the dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl, then whisk in the olive oil until thick and emulsified.
Spread the lettuce on a large platter. Arrange the beans, cherry tomatoes, olives and tuna in groups on top.
Add the egg quarters and drizzle with the dressing just before serving.

stages.title: Cook the eggs
steps: Half-fill a medium saucepan with water and bring to the boil over high heat.
Lower in the eggs and boil over medium-high heat for 9 minutes, until the yolks are firm and cooked through.
Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with cold water and ice. Transfer the eggs to the bowl with a spoon and cool for 5 minutes, then peel and cut into quarters.

stages.title: Blanch the beans
steps: Bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil over high heat.
Add the green beans and cook for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender with a slight bite.
Drain, then plunge into a bowl of cold water for 2 minutes to stop the cooking. Drain well and pat dry.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Put the dijon mustard, lemon juice, salt and black pepper in a small bowl.
Whisk in the olive oil, a little at a time, until the dressing is thick and emulsified.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Spread the lettuce over a large platter.
Arrange the green beans, cherry tomatoes, kalamata olives and tuna in separate groups on the lettuce.
Add the egg quarters, then drizzle with the dressing just before serving.

tips: Cooling the eggs in iced water stops the cooking, which prevents a grey ring around the yolk and makes them easier to peel.
Draining the beans well after blanching stops water diluting the dressing.
Tuna in olive oil is richer and more tender than tuna in brine, so it flakes into soft chunks on the platter.
Dress the salad just before serving so the lettuce stays crisp.
variations: Add 400 g boiled and sliced waxy potatoes, tossed in a spoonful of the dressing while warm.
Swap the canned tuna for 4 seared salmon fillets, cooked over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes each side until the flesh flakes easily.
storage: Keep the components separate in the fridge for up to 1 day and dress just before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Chilaquiles verdes
summary: Crisp tortilla triangles softened in tangy green salsa, topped with fried eggs, crema and fresh coriander.
ingredients: 8 corn tortillas, each cut into 6 triangles
1 jalapenos, halved and seeded for less heat
1 onion, half roughly chopped, half finely diced
1 bunch coriander, stems and leaves separated, leaves roughly chopped
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the tortilla triangles with 1 tbsp of the olive oil on two lined trays and bake for 12–15 minutes, until golden and crisp. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt.

Put the tomatillos, jalapeno, roughly chopped onion, garlic and coriander stems in a saucepan with 250 ml water. Bring to the boil over high heat, then simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes, until soft and dull olive green.
Blend the lot with the cooking liquid until smooth, then season with the remaining salt.

Simmer the sauce in a large frying pan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened. Toss through the tortillas for 1 minute, until coated but still partly crisp, then divide among 4 plates.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks runny. Top each plate with an egg.
Scatter over the finely diced onion and coriander leaves, then spoon over the sour cream and serve.

stages.title: Bake the tortilla triangles
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Spread the tortilla triangles in a single layer on the trays and toss with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp.
Sprinkle with a pinch of the salt and set aside.

stages.title: Simmer and blend the green sauce
steps: Put the tomatillos, jalapenos, the roughly chopped half of the onion, the garlic and the coriander stems in a medium saucepan with 250 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes, until the tomatillos are soft and dull olive green.
Tip into a blender with the cooking liquid and blend until smooth.
Stir in the remaining salt, tasting as you go.

stages.title: Reduce the sauce and toss
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium heat and pour in the blended tomatillo sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened and coating the back of a spoon.
Add the baked tortilla triangles and toss for 1 minute, until coated but with some edges still crisp.
Remove from the heat and divide among 4 plates.

stages.title: Fry the eggs and serve
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Crack in the eggs and fry for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are runny, or cooked through if you prefer.
Top each plate with an egg, then scatter over the finely diced onion and the coriander leaves.
Spoon the sour cream over the top and serve straight away.

tips: Baking the tortillas rather than frying keeps them dry and sturdy, so they hold some crunch under the sauce.
Simmer the tomatillos only until soft; overcooking dulls the sauce's bright, tangy flavour.
Toss the triangles through the sauce just before serving, because they soften within minutes.
Slightly stale tortillas crisp better than fresh ones because they have less moisture to bake off.
variations: Stir shredded cooked chicken through the sauce with the tortilla triangles for a heartier brunch.
Swap the sour cream for crumbled feta for a saltier, sharper finish.
storage: Keep leftover green sauce in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days and reheat gently in a pan. Assembled chilaquiles are best eaten straight away as the tortilla goes soft.

title: Batata harra
summary: Crisp roasted potatoes tossed with garlic, coriander, chilli and fresh lemon for a lively mezze side.
ingredients: 800 g potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 bunch coriander, leaves and tender stems roughly chopped
method: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) with a large baking tray inside. Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes, then chop the garlic and coriander and halve the lemon.
Cover the potatoes with cold water, add 1 tsp of the salt and bring to the boil on high. Reduce to medium and simmer 6–8 minutes, until the edges are soft but the cubes hold their shape.
Drain well and steam dry for 3 minutes, shaking to roughen the edges. Toss with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Tip onto the hot tray in a single layer and roast 20 minutes. Turn and roast another 12–15 minutes, until deep golden and crisp outside and tender inside.
Warm the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a small pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Cook the garlic and chilli flakes for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant and pale golden, then take off the heat.
Toss the hot potatoes with the garlic and chilli oil, coriander and lemon juice. Serve straight away, with chilli oil if you like.

stages.title: Prepare the potatoes and herbs
steps: Peel the potatoes if you like, then cut them into 2 cm cubes so they cook evenly.
Finely chop the garlic and roughly chop the coriander leaves and tender stems.
Halve the lemon and set it aside, ready for juicing at the end.
Put the potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold water by about 3 cm.

stages.title: Parboil the potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and put a large baking tray inside to heat.
Add 1 tsp of the salt to the pot, bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are soft but the cubes still hold their shape.
Drain well in a colander and leave to steam dry for 3 minutes, shaking the colander once or twice to roughen the edges.

stages.title: Roast until crisp
steps: Toss the dry potatoes with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Carefully tip them onto the hot tray in a single layer and roast for 20 minutes.
Turn the potatoes with a spatula and roast for another 12–15 minutes, until deep golden and crisp on the outside and tender in the middle.

stages.title: Fry the garlic and chilli, then toss
steps: While the potatoes finish, warm the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook, stirring, for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant and the garlic is just pale golden. Take off the heat straight away so it doesn't turn bitter.
Tip the hot potatoes into a large bowl, pour over the garlic and chilli oil, add the coriander and squeeze in the juice of the lemon. Toss and serve immediately.

tips: Parboiling and drying the potatoes before roasting gives a fluffy centre and a rough surface that crisps well in the oven.
Preheating the tray means the potatoes start sizzling the moment they land, which helps stop them sticking.
Adding the garlic to the oil at the end, not the oven, keeps its flavour fresh and avoids burnt, bitter bits.
Adding the coriander and lemon off the heat keeps the herbs bright and stops the potatoes going soggy while they wait.
variations: Stir through 1 tsp ground cumin with the garlic and chilli for a warmer, earthier flavour.
Swap the lemon juice for 1 tbsp pomegranate molasses if you have it, for a sweeter tang.
storage: Best eaten straight away while crisp. Leftovers keep in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat on a tray in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 10 minutes until hot and crisp.

title: Zuppa Toscana
summary: A hearty Tuscan-style soup of sausage, potatoes and kale in a lightly creamy garlic broth.
ingredients: 400 g potatoes, halved lengthways and sliced 5 mm thick
150 g kale, stems removed and leaves roughly torn
method: Squeeze the sausages from their casings. Finely chop the onion and garlic, slice the potatoes 5 mm thick and tear the kale.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage meat for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and no longer pink.
Reduce to medium and cook the onion for 3–4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, stock and water, scraping up the browned bits. Boil on high, then simmer partly covered on medium-low for 12–15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 4–5 minutes until wilted. Add the cream and warm for 2–3 minutes until steaming, without boiling.
Season with the salt and pepper, taste and adjust, then serve hot.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and sausage
steps: Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings and discard the casings.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Slice the potatoes 5 mm thick, halving them lengthways first if large.
Strip the kale leaves from the stems and tear the leaves into bite-sized pieces.

stages.title: Brown the sausage and soften the onion
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Add the sausage meat and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it into small chunks with a wooden spoon, until browned and no longer pink.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion and cook in the rendered fat for 3–4 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes, chicken stock and 250 ml water to the pot and stir, scraping up any browned bits from the base.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Simmer, partly covered, for 12–15 minutes until the potato slices are tender when pierced with a knife.

stages.title: Add the kale and cream
steps: Stir in the kale and simmer over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes until wilted and tender.
Pour in the thickened cream and warm for 2–3 minutes until steaming, without letting it boil.
Season with the salt and black pepper, then taste and add more if needed.
Ladle into bowls and serve hot.

tips: Browning the sausage well builds flavour, and the rendered fat then seasons the onion and the broth.
Slicing the potatoes evenly at 5 mm means they cook at the same rate and a few break down slightly to thicken the soup.
Keep the soup below a boil once the cream goes in, as boiling can make the cream split and look grainy.
Add the kale after the potatoes so it stays tender and green rather than turning dull and soft.
variations: Use hot Italian-style sausages and double the chilli flakes for a spicier soup.
Swap the kale for cavolo nero, cooking it for 6–7 minutes until tender.
storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pot over medium-low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if too thick. Not ideal to freeze as the potato and cream can turn grainy.

title: Egg drop soup
summary: Silky ribbons of egg swirl through a light ginger-scented broth with spring onions and white pepper.
method: Slice the ginger and spring onions, keeping the spring onions separate. Beat the eggs in a jug, and mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Put the stock, 250 ml water and ginger in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then simmer gently on medium-low for 8 minutes.
Remove the ginger, then season with the pepper and salt.
Return to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir in the cornflour mixture and cook for 1 minute until glossy and slightly thickened.
Reduce to low and swirl the soup. Pour in the eggs in a thin stream, then leave for 30 seconds until the ribbons are set and opaque.
Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and most of the spring onions. Ladle into bowls and top with the rest.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Thinly slice the ginger and spring onions, keeping the spring onions separate.
Crack the eggs into a jug and beat lightly with a fork until the yolks and whites are just combined.
Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth.

stages.title: Infuse the stock
steps: Pour the chicken stock and 250 ml water into a medium saucepan and add the ginger.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Lift out the ginger with a slotted spoon and discard it.
Stir in the black pepper and the salt.

stages.title: Thicken and add the egg
steps: Return the stock to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Stir the cornflour mixture again, then pour it in while stirring, and cook for 1 minute until the soup turns slightly glossy and thickens.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir the soup in one slow circular direction to create a gentle swirl.
Pour the beaten eggs in a thin stream into the moving soup, then stop stirring and leave for 30 seconds until the egg ribbons are set and opaque.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and most of the spring onions.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the remaining spring onions.

tips: A thin, slow stream of egg into moving soup makes fine silky ribbons, while pouring it in fast gives clumps.
Keep the soup at a gentle simmer when adding the egg, because a hard boil breaks the egg into small cloudy bits.
The cornflour thickens the broth just enough to suspend the egg, so stir the slurry again right before adding it as it settles quickly.
Add the sesame oil off the heat, as it loses its aroma when cooked.
variations: Add 1 cup of corn kernels with the stock and simmer for 3 minutes for a sweet corn version.
Stir in 100 g of sliced mushrooms with the ginger and simmer until tender for extra body.
storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat until steaming hot, without boiling.

title: Moroccan briouats with almonds
summary: Crisp triangular pastries filled with fragrant almond paste, cinnamon and orange blossom, dipped in honey.
method: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan). Mix the ground almonds, icing sugar, cinnamon, orange blossom water and 1 tbsp water into a firm, moist paste.
Cut the filo sheets lengthwise into 3 strips each, keeping them covered. Brush each strip with some of the melted butter and put 1 heaped teaspoon of paste at one end.
Fold each strip over the filling into a triangle, flag-style, to the end. Seal the loose end with butter and place seam-side down on a lined tray.
Brush the tops with the remaining butter. Bake for 15–18 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Warm the honey with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, until runny. Dip the warm triangles, then drain on a rack for 5 minutes, until tacky.

stages.title: Make the almond filling
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Combine the ground almonds, icing sugar and ground cinnamon in a bowl.
Add the orange blossom water and 1 tbsp water, then stir and press until the mixture forms a firm, moist paste that holds together when squeezed.

stages.title: Cut and fill the filo
steps: Stack the filo sheets and cover with a damp tea towel so they don't dry out. Lay 1 sheet on the bench and cut it lengthwise into 3 equal strips, keeping the rest covered.
Brush a strip lightly with melted butter, then place 1 heaped teaspoon of filling on one end, about 2 cm from the edge.
Repeat with the remaining sheets, working one sheet at a time, to make 24 strips.

stages.title: Fold the triangles
steps: Fold the corner of the filled end over the filling to form a triangle, then keep folding the strip over itself, flag-style, along its length until you reach the end.
Brush the loose end with butter and tuck it under to seal. Place seam-side down on the lined tray.
Brush the tops of all the triangles with the remaining melted butter.

stages.title: Bake until golden
steps: Bake the triangles on the middle shelf for 15–18 minutes, until deep golden and crisp all over.
Transfer to a wire rack placed over a tray.

stages.title: Dip in honey
steps: Warm the honey with 1 tbsp water in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, until runny but not boiling.
Dip each warm triangle briefly in the honey, turning once, and lift out with tongs.
Drain on the rack for 5 minutes, until the honey is tacky and no longer dripping.

tips: Keeping the filo under a damp tea towel stops the thin sheets drying and cracking when folded.
A firm, moist paste holds its shape inside the pastry and won't leak out during baking.
Dipping the pastries while still warm lets the honey cling lightly without making the filo soggy.
variations: Add the finely grated zest of 1 orange to the almond paste for a brighter citrus note.
Sprinkle the honeyed triangles with toasted sesame seeds before the honey sets.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. They soften over time, so re-crisp in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 5 minutes.

title: Colcannon
summary: Buttery mashed potatoes folded with tender cabbage and spring onions for a comforting Irish classic.
ingredients: 800 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
70 g butter, plus extra for serving
1 tsp salt, plus extra for the cooking water
method: Boil the potato chunks in salted water, bringing to the boil on high then simmering on medium for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam dry for 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, melt 20 g of the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the cabbage with 1/2 tsp of the salt for 5–6 minutes, until wilted but still bright green.
Add the spring onions, cook for 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat.
Warm the milk in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until steaming but not boiling.
Mash the potatoes with the remaining 50 g butter until smooth. Stir in the warm milk, pepper and remaining salt until creamy, then fold through the cabbage mixture.
Spoon into a warm bowl, make a well in the centre and melt a knob of extra butter in it.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 4 cm chunks so they cook evenly.
Remove the tough core from the cabbage and shred the leaves finely.
Thinly slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts together.

stages.title: Boil the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water and add a good pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.
Drain well in a colander and leave the potatoes to steam dry for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Cook the cabbage and milk
steps: While the potatoes simmer, melt 20 g of the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the cabbage and 1/2 tsp of the salt and cook, stirring, for 5–6 minutes, until wilted and tender but still bright green.
Add the spring onions and cook for 1 minute, then remove the pan from the heat.
Warm the milk in a small saucepan over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until steaming but not boiling.

stages.title: Mash and serve
steps: Return the dry potatoes to the pot and mash with the remaining 50 g butter until smooth.
Stir in the warm milk, the pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt until the mash is creamy.
Fold through the cabbage and spring onion mixture until evenly combined.
Spoon into a warm bowl, make a small well in the centre and add a knob of extra butter to melt.

tips: Letting the drained potatoes steam dry for 2 minutes stops the mash turning watery and lets it absorb the butter.
Warm milk keeps the mash hot and fluffy, while cold milk cools it and can make it gluey.
Cooking the cabbage in butter first removes its raw edge and gives a sweeter flavour than boiling it.
Mash by hand rather than in a food processor, which overworks the starch and makes the potato gluey.
variations: Swap the cabbage for shredded kale or cavolo nero, cooked for 1–2 minutes longer until tender.
Fry 3 rashers of chopped bacon until crisp and fold them through at the end for a smoky version.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of milk, stirring, until steaming hot.

title: Hiyayakko
summary: Chilled silken tofu topped with ginger, spring onions and soy for a clean, refreshing starter.
method: Refrigerate the silken tofu in its packet for at least 30 minutes until very cold, and chill four small plates alongside it.
Grate the ginger finely and lightly squeeze it, keeping the pulp and juice. Thinly slice the spring onions.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until light golden and fragrant, then cool on a plate.
Tip the tofu onto paper towel, blot dry and cut into four even pieces. Slide each onto a chilled plate.
Top each piece with the ginger and spring onions, scatter over the sesame seeds and drizzle with the soy sauce. Serve straight away while cold.

stages.title: Chill the tofu
steps: Leave the silken tofu in its sealed packet and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, until very cold.
Chill four small plates or shallow bowls in the fridge at the same time.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Peel the ginger and grate it finely, then squeeze lightly to release a little juice and keep both the pulp and juice.
Slice the spring onions as thinly as you can.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, shaking the pan, until light golden and fragrant, then tip onto a plate to cool.

stages.title: Cut and plate the tofu
steps: Open the packet and carefully tip out the tofu onto a board lined with paper towel, then gently blot away the surface liquid.
Dip a sharp knife in water and cut the block into four even pieces.
Slide each piece onto a chilled plate with a spatula, keeping the pieces whole.

stages.title: Dress and serve
steps: Pile the grated ginger and spring onions on top of each piece of tofu.
Scatter over the toasted sesame seeds.
Drizzle 1½ tsp of the soy sauce over each portion and serve straight away, while the tofu is still cold.

tips: Silken tofu is very delicate, so cutting it with a wet knife stops it sticking and tearing.
Chilled plates keep the tofu cold, which is the whole point of this dish on a warm day.
Dress with the soy sauce just before serving, because it draws water from the tofu and the plate turns watery if it sits.
Grate the ginger on the finest grater so it melts into the soy rather than leaving stringy bits.
variations: Replace the sesame seeds with a spoonful of crushed peanuts and add a few drops of sesame oil for a richer finish.
Add a few thin slices of cucumber or a little chilli flakes on top for crunch or heat.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftover plain tofu can be kept covered in the fridge for 1 day, but dress it only when serving.

title: Pão de queijo (cheese bread)
summary: Chewy, golden cheese rolls made with tapioca starch and Parmesan, crisp outside and stretchy within.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Brush a 12-hole mini muffin tin with 1 tsp of the oil and tip the tapioca starch into a large heatproof bowl.
Heat the milk, remaining oil and salt in a small saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Don't let it boil hard.
Pour the hot liquid over the starch and mix until no dry patches remain and it looks shaggy and slightly translucent. Cool for about 10 minutes, until warm to the touch.
Beat in the egg for 2–3 minutes until the dough is smooth and very sticky, then mix in the parmesan until stretchy.
With wet hands, roll the dough into 12 golf-ball-sized balls and place one in each muffin hole.
Bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and set. Rest in the tin for 3 minutes, then serve warm.

stages.title: Heat the oven and prepare the tin
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Brush a 12-hole mini muffin tin with 1 tsp of the vegetable oil, keeping the remaining oil for the dough.
Tip the tapioca starch into a large heatproof bowl.

stages.title: Scald the starch
steps: Combine the milk, the remaining vegetable oil and the salt in a small saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles form around the edge. Do not let it boil hard.
Pour the hot liquid over the tapioca starch and stir with a wooden spoon until no dry patches remain and the mixture looks shaggy and slightly translucent.

stages.title: Cool and finish the dough
steps: Leave the mixture to cool for about 10 minutes, until warm to the touch rather than hot, so it won't cook the egg.
Add the egg and beat vigorously with the spoon or your hands for 2–3 minutes, until the egg is absorbed and the dough is smooth and very sticky.
Add the parmesan and mix until evenly combined and stretchy.
Wet your hands and roll the dough into 12 balls about the size of a golf ball, then place one in each muffin hole.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake on the middle shelf for 20–22 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and set. They should feel light, with a crisp shell and a soft, chewy centre.
Rest in the tin for 3 minutes, then lift out and serve warm.

tips: Letting the scalded mixture cool before adding the egg stops the egg scrambling and keeps the dough smooth.
Finely grated parmesan melts into the dough evenly; coarse shreds leave pockets that leak and brown too fast.
Wet hands stop the sticky dough clinging to your fingers when you roll the balls.
Serve warm, as the centres go dense once cold; a quick re-bake brings back the crisp shell.
variations: Replace half the parmesan with grated mozzarella for a stretchier, milder centre.
Add 1 tsp finely chopped chives or a pinch of chilli flakes to the dough with the cheese.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat on a tray in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 6–8 minutes, until hot and crisp outside. Raw shaped balls can be frozen and baked from frozen for 5–8 minutes longer.

title: Pasta e ceci
summary: Chickpeas and small pasta simmered in a rosemary-scented tomato broth until thick and comforting.
ingredients: 180 g pasta, ditalini or other small shapes
method: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, setting aside 1/2 cup for garnish. Finely chop the onion and garlic, and chop the rosemary leaves.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and salt for 8–10 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the passata, remaining chickpeas and stock, then boil on high. Simmer on medium-low, partly covered, for 15 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Blend about 2 cups of chickpeas with some liquid until smooth, then stir back into the pot.
Simmer on medium, add the pasta and cook 8–10 minutes until al dente and thick. Season with pepper and extra salt, then rest off the heat for 2 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved chickpeas, remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the parmesan, if using.

stages.title: Prepare the base
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas well under cold running water, then set aside about 1/2 cup for garnish.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Strip the rosemary leaves from the sprig and chop them finely.

stages.title: Soften the aromatics
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the onion and the salt, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook, stirring, for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the chickpeas
steps: Add the passata, the larger portion of chickpeas and the vegetable stock, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Scoop out about 2 cups of the chickpeas and some liquid, blend with a stick blender or in a jug blender until smooth, then stir back into the pot.

stages.title: Cook the pasta
steps: Return the soup to a steady simmer over medium heat and add the pasta, stirring well.
Cook for 8–10 minutes, or according to the packet, stirring often so the pasta doesn't stick, until the pasta is al dente and the soup is thick; add a splash of hot water if it becomes too thick.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Remove from the heat and rest for 2 minutes so the soup thickens slightly.
Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved chickpeas, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the parmesan, if using.

tips: Blending some of the chickpeas makes the broth creamy without any cream, giving the soup its traditional body.
Cooking the onion slowly without browning keeps the flavour sweet and balances the acidity of the passata.
The pasta keeps absorbing liquid as it rests, so serve promptly and loosen with hot water if the soup gets too thick.
Check the label on parmesan if serving vegetarians, as it is made with animal rennet.
variations: Stir in a handful of chopped silverbeet or kale for the last 5 minutes of cooking for added greens.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for a gentle heat.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The pasta will swell, so add a splash of water or stock when reheating over medium heat until steaming hot. Not ideal to freeze once the pasta is added.

title: Nopales salad
summary: Tender cactus paddles tossed with tomatoes, onion, coriander and lime for a tangy fresh salad.
ingredients: 400 g cleaned nopales, cut into 1 cm strips
1 bunch coriander, leaves and stems finely chopped
method: Rinse the nopales. Finely chop the tomatoes, red onion and coriander, then juice the limes. Put the tomato and onion in a large bowl.
Boil 2 litres water with 1 tbsp salt in a large saucepan over high heat. Add the nopales, reduce to medium and simmer 12–15 minutes, until tender but slightly firm and bright olive green.
Drain, rinse under cold water until no longer slippery, then pat dry. Spread on a tray for 15 minutes, until completely cool.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, black pepper and half the coriander. Toss through the nopales, tomato and onion.
Cover and chill for 15 minutes. Scatter over the remaining coriander and serve cold.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Rinse the nopales strips under cold running water and drain well.
Finely chop the tomatoes and red onion and place them in a large bowl.
Finely chop the coriander and set aside half for the dressing, keeping the other half for serving.
Juice the limes to get about 80 ml juice.

stages.title: Simmer the nopales
steps: Bring 2 litres water and the 1 tbsp salt to the boil in a large saucepan over high heat.
Add the nopales, reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until tender but still slightly firm and bright olive green.
Drain in a colander and rinse well under cold water until the slippery coating is gone.
Drain again and pat dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Cool the nopales
steps: Spread the nopales on a tray in a single layer.
Leave for 15 minutes until completely cool, so they don't wilt the tomato and onion.

stages.title: Dress and chill
steps: Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt, black pepper and half the coriander in a small bowl.
Add the cooled nopales to the tomato and onion, pour over the dressing and toss to coat.
Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes so the flavours mingle.
Scatter the remaining coriander over the salad and serve cold.

tips: Rinsing the cooked nopales well removes the sticky coating, so the salad stays crisp rather than slimy.
Cooling the nopales completely before dressing keeps the tomato firm and the lime juice tasting fresh.
Salting the cooking water seasons the nopales through, so the dressing needs only a little salt.
Cutting the strips to an even thickness means they all cook tender in the same time.
variations: Add 1 diced avocado and 100 g crumbled feta just before serving for a richer salad.
Stir in 1 finely chopped red chilli with the onion for a hotter version.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Serve cold; it is not suitable to freeze.

title: Gougères
summary: Airy choux pastry puffs with nutty Gruyère and a delicate crisp shell.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two trays with baking paper. Grate the gruyere, reserving 2 tbsp for the top, and sift the flour.
Bring the water, milk, butter and salt to a rolling boil in a saucepan over medium heat. Off the heat, beat in the flour until smooth and the paste leaves the sides of the pan.
Cook the paste over low heat for 1–2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the base. Cool in a bowl for 5 minutes, until warm.
Beat in the whisked eggs in 3 batches until glossy and the paste falls in a thick ribbon. Stir in the gruyere, nutmeg and black pepper.
Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays, 4 cm apart. Sprinkle with the reserved cheese, bake 10 minutes, then at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15–20 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.
Pierce each gougère with a skewer, then dry out in the switched-off oven for 5 minutes. Serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare the trays and cheese
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Finely grate 120 g gruyere, then set aside 2 tbsp of it for sprinkling on top.
Sift the flour onto a sheet of baking paper so it can be tipped into the pan in one go.

stages.title: Cook the choux paste
steps: Combine the water, milk, butter and salt in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring until the butter melts, then bring to a rolling boil.
Remove the pan from the heat and tip in the flour all at once. Beat hard with a wooden spoon until the mixture is smooth and comes away from the sides of the pan.
Return the pan to low heat and stir for 1–2 minutes, until a thin film forms on the base of the pan.
Transfer the paste to a bowl and cool for 5 minutes, until warm but not hot.

stages.title: Beat in the eggs and cheese
steps: Lightly whisk the eggs in a jug. Beat about one-third into the paste until fully combined and glossy.
Add the remaining egg in 2 more batches, beating well each time, until the paste is smooth and falls slowly from the spoon in a thick ribbon. You may not need all the egg.
Stir in the grated gruyere (except the reserved 2 tbsp), the nutmeg and a few grinds of black pepper.

stages.title: Pipe and bake
steps: Spoon the mixture into a piping bag with a 1 cm plain nozzle, or use two spoons. Pipe or spoon walnut-sized mounds onto the trays, 4 cm apart.
Dab down any peaks with a wet finger, then sprinkle the reserved cheese over the tops.
Bake for 10 minutes without opening the oven door. Reduce the temperature to 180°C (160°C fan) and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until puffed, deep golden and crisp.
Pierce the side of each gougere with a skewer to release steam, then return to the switched-off oven for 5 minutes to dry out. Serve warm.

tips: Beat the eggs in gradually: too much egg makes a loose paste that spreads and won't puff, so stop when it drops slowly from the spoon.
Cooking the paste briefly on the heat dries it out, which gives a crisper shell and a better rise.
Keep the oven door shut for the first 10 minutes, as the steam that lifts the puffs collapses if the oven cools.
Finely grated cheese melts evenly into the paste without blocking the piping nozzle.
variations: Replace the nutmeg with 1 tsp dijon mustard beaten in with the cheese for a sharper flavour.
Use cheddar cheese instead of gruyere and add 1 tbsp chopped chives.
storage: Store cooled gougeres in an airtight container for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat at 180°C (160°C fan) for 5–8 minutes until crisp and hot through.

title: Hobak jeon
summary: Tender courgette rounds coated in a light egg batter and pan-fried until delicately golden.
method: Lay the zucchini rounds on paper towel, sprinkle with the salt and leave for 10 minutes. Pat both sides dry.
Spread the flour in one shallow dish and beat the eggs in another.
Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl for the dipping sauce.
Heat some of the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frypan over medium heat. Dip each round in the flour, then the egg.
Fry in batches in a single layer for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and the egg is set. Wipe the pan and add more oil before each batch.
Serve the jeon warm with the dipping sauce.

stages.title: Salt the zucchini
steps: Cut the zucchini into 5 mm rounds and lay them in a single layer on a tray lined with paper towel.
Sprinkle the rounds evenly with the salt and leave for 10 minutes to draw out moisture.
Pat both sides of each round dry with more paper towel.

stages.title: Set up the coating and dipping sauce
steps: Spread the plain flour in a shallow dish.
Lightly beat the eggs in a second shallow dish until the yolks and whites are combined.
Stir the soy sauce and rice vinegar together in a small bowl to make the dipping sauce.

stages.title: Coat and pan-fry
steps: Heat 2 teaspoons of the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frypan over medium heat.
Dip each zucchini round in the flour, shake off the excess, then coat in the egg.
Fry a batch in a single layer for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and the egg is set.
Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate, then wipe the pan and add 2 teaspoons more oil before each of the remaining batches, cooking all rounds the same way.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Arrange the warm jeon on a plate.
Serve with the soy and rice vinegar dipping sauce.

tips: Salting and drying the zucchini removes water, so the egg coating sticks and the rounds fry golden instead of steaming.
Shake off excess flour before dipping, or the coating turns pasty and peels away in the pan.
Keep the heat at medium; higher heat browns the egg before the zucchini softens.
variations: Add 1 finely sliced red chilli and a pinch of sesame seeds to the dipping sauce for heat and nuttiness.
Use rounds of eggplant cut 8 mm thick, frying 3–4 minutes per side until tender.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frypan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes per side until hot through; the coating will be softer than when fresh.

title: Chè ba màu (three-colour dessert)
summary: Colourful layers of sweet beans, pandan jelly and coconut milk served over crushed ice.
ingredients: 150 g pandan jelly, cut into 1 cm strips
method: Simmer the red beans with 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, until syrupy and glossy. Cool in a bowl.
Cook the mung beans the same way with 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water, keeping them whole, until the liquid thickens and coats them. Cool in a bowl.
Whisk the cornflour with 2 tbsp water, then add the coconut milk, remaining sugar and salt. Heat over medium for 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened, without boiling hard, then cool for 5 minutes.
Cover and chill the beans and coconut sauce for at least 20 minutes, until cold. Keep the pandan jelly strips in the fridge.
Layer the mung beans, red beans and pandan jelly in 4 tall glasses, pack in the crushed ice, then pour over the cold sauce and serve straight away.

stages.title: Sweeten the red beans
steps: Combine the red beans, 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water in a small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid is syrupy and the beans are glossy.
Tip into a bowl and leave to cool to room temperature.

stages.title: Sweeten the mung beans
steps: Combine the mung beans, 3 tbsp of the sugar and 100 ml water in a second small saucepan.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring gently so the beans stay whole, until the liquid has thickened and coated them.
Tip into a bowl and leave to cool to room temperature.

stages.title: Make the coconut sauce
steps: Whisk the cornflour with 2 tbsp water in a small saucepan until smooth, then add the coconut milk, the remaining sugar and the salt.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon. Do not let it boil hard.
Pour into a jug and cool for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Chill the components
steps: Cover the red beans, mung beans and coconut sauce separately.
Refrigerate for at least 20 minutes, until cold.
Keep the pandan jelly strips in the fridge until assembling.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Divide the mung beans among 4 tall glasses, then add a layer of red beans.
Top with the pandan jelly strips.
Pack in the crushed ice, pressing it down lightly.
Pour the cold coconut sauce over the ice and serve straight away with long spoons, stirring the layers together as you eat.

tips: Cooking each bean separately keeps the colours distinct and lets you control how sweet each layer is.
Cornflour gives the coconut sauce body so it clings to the ice instead of sinking and diluting.
Chilling every component first slows the ice melting, so the dessert stays thick rather than watery.
Simmer the mung beans gently, because hard bubbling breaks them up and clouds the layer.
variations: Swap the pandan jelly for grass jelly or cubes of mango.
Top with roasted crushed peanuts for crunch.
storage: Keep the beans, jelly and coconut sauce in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Assemble with fresh ice just before serving.

title: Sbrisolona
summary: Crumbly almond shortbread from Mantua with a sandy texture and buttery toasted edges.
ingredients: 150 g almonds, finely chopped, or ground almonds
170 g cold butter, cut into 1 cm cubes, plus extra for greasing
method: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan). Grease a 24 cm springform tin with a little extra butter and line the base with baking paper.
Combine the flour, polenta, almonds, sugar, lemon zest and salt in a large bowl.
Rub in the cold butter until you have coarse, uneven crumbs with some pea-sized lumps.
Toss through the egg yolks with a fork until the mixture clumps in places but stays crumbly. Don't knead it smooth.
Scatter the crumbs loosely into the tin and press very lightly, keeping the surface rough. Bake in the centre for 35–40 minutes, until deep golden with lightly browned edges and a dry, set centre.
Cool in the tin for 30 minutes, then remove the side and break into rustic pieces.

stages.title: Prepare the tin and oven
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan).
Grease a 24 cm round springform tin with a little extra butter and line the base with baking paper.

stages.title: Make the crumb mixture
steps: Combine the plain flour, polenta, almonds, caster sugar, lemon zest and salt in a large bowl.
Add the cold butter and rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture forms coarse, uneven crumbs with some pea-sized lumps.
Add the egg yolks and toss through with a fork until the mixture clumps in places but stays crumbly. Do not knead it smooth.

stages.title: Fill the tin
steps: Scatter the crumbs loosely into the prepared tin.
Press very lightly with your palm so the surface is just even, keeping the texture rough.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Bake in the centre of the oven for 35–40 minutes, until deep golden on top and the edges are lightly browned.
Check that the centre looks dry and set, with no pale, raw patches.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool the cake in the tin for 30 minutes so it firms up and can be handled.
Remove the side of the tin and break the sbrisolona into rustic pieces with your hands or the back of a knife.

tips: Cold butter rubbed in unevenly gives the crumbly, short texture the cake is known for. Warm butter makes it dense and greasy.
Leave the mixture lumpy and press only lightly, because overworking it forms a smooth dough and loses the crunchy crumb.
Polenta adds the characteristic grit and crunch. Use fine or regular polenta, not instant, for the best bite.
Cooling in the tin lets the butter set, so the cake breaks into pieces rather than collapsing into loose crumbs.
variations: Replace 50 g of the almonds with roughly chopped hazelnuts for a toastier flavour.
Add 1 tsp vanilla extract with the egg yolks for a softer, rounder flavour.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Keep it dry, as it softens in the fridge.

title: Bakewell tart
summary: Buttery pastry layered with raspberry jam and almond frangipane, finished with flaked almonds.
ingredients: 1 sheet shortcrust pastry (about 25 cm square), thawed
1 cup rice, uncooked, for weighing down the pastry (or baking beads)
method: Press the pastry into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, prick the base and chill for 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Line the pastry with baking paper and the rice. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the paper and rice, then bake 5 minutes more until pale golden and dry.
Beat the butter and caster sugar for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the almond meal and flour.
Spread the jam over the warm case, spoon the frangipane on top and smooth it to the edge. Scatter with the flaked almonds.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean. Foil the edge if it browns too fast.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then remove and dust with the icing sugar.

stages.title: Line the tin and chill
steps: Press the pastry sheet into a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin, pushing it into the fluted edge and trimming the excess with a knife.
Prick the base all over with a fork.
Chill the lined tin in the fridge for 30 minutes so the pastry holds its shape.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) while the pastry chills.

stages.title: Blind-bake the case
steps: Line the chilled pastry with baking paper and fill with the uncooked rice.
Bake for 15 minutes, then lift out the paper and rice.
Bake the empty case for a further 5 minutes until pale golden and dry, then cool in the tin for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the frangipane
steps: Beat the butter and caster sugar in a bowl with electric beaters for 3–4 minutes until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then add the vanilla extract; the mixture may look slightly curdled, which is fine.
Fold in the almond meal and plain flour until just combined.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Spread the raspberry jam evenly over the base of the warm pastry case.
Spoon the frangipane over the jam and smooth it to the edge, sealing it against the pastry.
Scatter the flaked almonds over the top.
Bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 30–35 minutes until deep golden and set, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Cover the edge with foil if the pastry browns too quickly.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Cool the tart in the tin for 10 minutes so the jam settles and it slices cleanly.
Remove from the tin and dust with the icing sugar before slicing.

tips: Blind-baking until dry keeps the base crisp under the wet jam and frangipane.
Spreading the jam on the warm case helps it go on evenly without tearing the pastry.
Sealing the frangipane against the pastry edge stops jam bubbling up the sides.
Resting the tart before slicing lets the filling firm up so the slices hold together.
variations: Swap the raspberry jam for cherry or apricot jam.
Add 1/2 tsp almond extract to the frangipane for a stronger almond flavour.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

title: Crema catalana
summary: Silky citrus-and-cinnamon custard topped with a brittle layer of caramelised sugar.
ingredients: 1 lemon, peel only, removed in wide strips
1 orange, peel only, removed in wide strips
method: Heat the milk, cinnamon stick, and lemon and orange peel in a saucepan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming. Steep for 10 minutes, then strain.
Whisk the egg yolks, 60 g of the caster sugar and the cornflour until pale and smooth. Slowly whisk in the warm milk.
Return to the clean pan over low heat. Stir for 6–8 minutes until thick and coating a spoon, then bubble gently for 1 minute.
Divide among four 150 ml ramekins. Cool for 20 minutes, cover the surfaces with plastic wrap, then chill for at least 3 hours until firm.
Blot the surfaces dry and sprinkle with the remaining 30 g sugar. Torch for 1–2 minutes per custard until deep golden, then rest 2 minutes to harden.

stages.title: Infuse the milk
steps: Remove the peel from the lemon and orange in wide strips with a vegetable peeler, avoiding the bitter white pith.
Combine the milk, cinnamon stick, lemon peel and orange peel in a medium saucepan.
Heat over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, then remove from the heat.
Cover and leave to steep for 10 minutes, then strain into a jug and discard the cinnamon and peel.

stages.title: Make the custard base
steps: Place the egg yolks, 60 g of the caster sugar and the cornflour in a medium heatproof bowl.
Whisk for 1–2 minutes until pale and smooth, with no lumps of cornflour.
Slowly pour in the warm infused milk while whisking constantly so the yolks do not scramble.

stages.title: Cook the custard
steps: Pour the mixture back into the clean saucepan and place over low heat.
Stir constantly with a whisk or wooden spoon, scraping the base and corners, for 6–8 minutes until it thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Let it bubble gently for 1 minute to cook out the cornflour, then remove from the heat.
Divide the custard among four 150 ml ramekins or shallow dishes.

stages.title: Chill until set
steps: Cool the ramekins on the bench for 20 minutes.
Cover the surface of each custard with plastic wrap to prevent a skin forming.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours until completely cold and firm.

stages.title: Caramelise and serve
steps: Remove the plastic wrap and blot any moisture from the surface with a paper towel.
Sprinkle the remaining 30 g caster sugar evenly over the custards in a thin layer.
Heat the sugar with a kitchen torch for 1–2 minutes per custard until melted and deep golden brown.
Rest for 2 minutes until the caramel hardens, then serve straight away.

tips: Stirring constantly over low heat stops the yolks scrambling and keeps the custard smooth.
Peel without white pith, as pith makes the infusion bitter.
Drying the surface before adding sugar helps it melt into an even, crisp layer instead of dissolving into a wet patch.
Caramelise just before serving; the crust softens as it sits on the custard.
variations: Add a strip of lime peel or a split vanilla bean to the milk for a different aroma.
Use a very hot grill instead of a torch, placing the ramekins in a tray of ice to keep the custard cold.
storage: Keep the uncaramelised custards covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Caramelise just before serving; do not freeze.

title: Skordalia
summary: A punchy garlic-and-potato dip whipped with olive oil and lemon until creamy and smooth.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
method: Peel and cut the potatoes into 3 cm chunks, then cover with cold water in a saucepan and add half the salt.
Pound the garlic with the remaining salt into a smooth, sticky paste with no visible pieces. Juice the lemon.
Bring the potatoes to the boil over high heat, then simmer on medium for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Drain, then leave the potatoes in the dry hot pan off the heat for 2 minutes to steam dry.
Mash until completely smooth, then mix in the garlic paste. Beat in the olive oil bit by bit until thick, creamy and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice and adjust the salt, then serve warm or at room temperature with a drizzle of extra oil.

stages.title: Prepare the potatoes
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even 3 cm chunks so they cook at the same rate.
Put the potatoes in a medium saucepan and cover with cold water by about 3 cm.
Add 1/2 tsp of the salt to the water.

stages.title: Make the garlic paste
steps: Put the garlic and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt in a mortar.
Pound with the pestle until it forms a smooth, sticky paste with no visible pieces, or crush it with the flat of a knife on a board.
Juice the lemon and set the juice aside.

stages.title: Boil the potatoes
steps: Bring the potatoes to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance and the edges begin to crumble.
Drain well in a colander.
Return the potatoes to the dry hot pan off the heat for 2 minutes so the steam escapes and they dry out.

stages.title: Mash and beat in the flavours
steps: Mash the warm potatoes with a masher or potato ricer until completely smooth.
Stir in the garlic paste until evenly combined.
Beat in the olive oil a tablespoon at a time, waiting until each addition is absorbed, until the mixture is thick, creamy and glossy.
Stir in the lemon juice, then taste and add a little more salt or lemon if needed. Stop mixing as soon as it is smooth, as overworking turns it gluey.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Spoon the skordalia into a shallow bowl and drizzle with a little extra olive oil if you like.
Serve warm or at room temperature with fried or roasted vegetables, or grilled fish.

tips: Dry the drained potatoes in the hot pan, because leftover water makes the skordalia loose and stops it absorbing the oil.
Mash the potatoes while still hot, as cold potato turns gluey and hard to smooth out.
Add the oil slowly so it emulsifies into the potato, giving a creamy rather than greasy texture.
Pounding the garlic with salt breaks it down fully, which avoids harsh raw chunks in the finished dip.
variations: Replace half the potato with 100 g of soaked, squeezed day-old bread for a more traditional, lighter skordalia.
Stir in 50 g of finely ground walnuts or almonds with the oil for a nutty, richer version.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Bring to room temperature and stir in a splash of olive oil or water to loosen before serving. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Causa limeña
summary: Chilled lime-and-chilli mashed potato layers filled with creamy tuna and avocado.
ingredients: 800 g yellow potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
2 x 185 g cans canned tuna, drained
method: Boil the potatoes with half the salt over high heat, then simmer on medium for 15–18 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam dry for 3 minutes.
Mash the warm potatoes until smooth. Mix in the juice of 2 limes, aji amarillo paste, olive oil and remaining salt, then knead until it holds together like soft dough.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, spring onions, juice of the last lime and black pepper in a bowl until creamy.
Line a 20 cm square dish or four 9 cm ring moulds with baking paper or plastic wrap. Press in half the potato, then top with the tuna filling and avocado slices.
Press the remaining potato over the top and smooth it. Refrigerate for at least 45 minutes until firm and cold.
Lift out, cut into 4 portions with a clean sharp knife and serve cold.

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, add 1/2 tsp of the salt and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 15–18 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.
Drain well and let the potatoes steam dry in the colander for 3 minutes.

stages.title: Make the potato layer
steps: Mash the warm potatoes until completely smooth, or push them through a potato ricer.
Squeeze the juice of 2 limes and stir it into the potato with the aji amarillo paste, olive oil and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.
Taste and add more salt if needed, then knead briefly until the mixture is smooth and holds together like a soft dough.

stages.title: Make the tuna filling
steps: Combine the tuna, mayonnaise, spring onions, the juice of the remaining lime and black pepper in a bowl.
Flake the tuna with a fork and mix until creamy.

stages.title: Layer the causa
steps: Line a 20 cm square dish or four 9 cm ring moulds with baking paper or plastic wrap, leaving some overhang.
Press half the potato mixture into the base in an even layer, smoothing the top with a wet spoon.
Spread the tuna filling over the potato, then arrange the avocado slices on top.
Press the remaining potato mixture over the avocado and smooth the surface.

stages.title: Chill and serve
steps: Cover and refrigerate for at least 45 minutes, until the causa is firm and cold.
Lift out using the overhang or slide off the moulds, cut into 4 portions with a sharp knife wiped clean between cuts, and serve cold.

tips: Mash the potatoes while hot, as cooled potato turns gluey and will not give a smooth layer.
Yellow, waxy-fleshed potatoes such as Nicola or Gold give the right buttery colour and texture; floury varieties can turn crumbly.
Wetting your spoon or hands stops the potato sticking when you smooth the layers.
Squeeze out the tuna well so the filling does not make the layers wet and slippery.
variations: Replace the tuna with shredded cooked chicken mixed with mayonnaise and a little extra lime juice.
Add a layer of finely diced tomato or sliced hard-boiled egg between the tuna and avocado.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Serve cold; do not freeze, as the potato turns grainy and the avocado browns.

title: Chawanmushi
summary: Delicate savoury egg custard steamed with dashi, mushrooms and prawns until barely set.
ingredients: 450 ml dashi stock, cooled to room temperature
4 shiitake mushrooms, stems removed and caps thinly sliced
100 g cooked prawns, peeled and roughly chopped
method: Gently whisk the eggs, then stir in the cooled dashi, soy sauce and mirin. Strain through a fine sieve into a clean jug.
Heat the oil in a small frying pan over medium heat. Cook the shiitake for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly golden, then cool briefly.
Divide the mushrooms and prawns among four 200 ml heatproof cups, pour in the strained custard and skim off any bubbles.
Cover each cup tightly with foil. Bring 2 cm of water to the boil in a lidded pan or wok with a rack, then reduce to low.
Steam the cups with the lid slightly ajar for 15–20 minutes, until just set with a slight wobble and the juices run clear.
Rest the cups for 3 minutes, scatter over the spring onion and serve warm.

stages.title: Prepare the custard base
steps: Crack the eggs into a jug and whisk gently with a fork, lifting the fork rather than beating, so no foam forms.
Stir in the cooled dashi stock, the soy sauce and the mirin until combined.
Pour the mixture through a fine sieve into a clean jug to remove any stringy egg white and bubbles.

stages.title: Cook the mushrooms and fill the cups
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a small frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the sliced shiitake mushrooms, stirring often, for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly golden, then cool for 2 minutes.
Divide the mushrooms and chopped prawns among four heatproof cups or ramekins of about 200 ml capacity.
Pour the strained custard evenly over the fillings, skimming off any surface bubbles with a spoon.

stages.title: Steam the custards
steps: Cover each cup tightly with foil to stop condensation dripping onto the custard.
Bring about 2 cm of water to a boil in a large lidded pan or wok, then set a steaming rack inside and reduce the heat to low so the water barely simmers.

Stand the cups on the rack, cover with the lid slightly ajar, and steam for 15–20 minutes until the custard is just set with a slight wobble and the juices run clear when a skewer is inserted in the centre.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Lift the cups out carefully and rest them for 3 minutes, uncovered.
Scatter the sliced spring onion over the top and serve warm with a spoon.

tips: Straining the egg mixture gives a silky, smooth custard because it removes strings of egg white and trapped air.
Cool the dashi before mixing, as hot stock will partly cook the eggs and leave the custard lumpy.
Keep the water at a bare simmer; a hard boil makes tiny holes and a rubbery texture in the custard.
Leaving the lid slightly ajar lets some steam escape, which keeps the temperature gentle and the surface smooth.
variations: Replace the prawns with 100 g shredded cooked chicken thigh and add a few blanched edamame to each cup.
Top each cooked custard with a spoonful of thickened dashi, made by simmering 100 ml dashi with 1 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornflour mixed with a little water until glossy.
storage: Cool, cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, covered, in a steamer for 5–8 minutes until hot through. Don't freeze.

title: Sabudana khichdi
summary: Tender tapioca pearls tossed with cumin, peanuts, potatoes and lime for a lightly spiced breakfast.
ingredients: 1 potato, peeled and cut into 1 cm dice
method: Rinse the sabudana pearls until the water runs almost clear, then soak in 200 ml water for 4 hours until soft. Drain and rest for 15 minutes.
Dice the potato, chop the chilli and coriander, and crush the peanuts. Toss the pearls with the peanuts and salt.
Heat the ghee in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the potato and cook for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender. Stir in the chilli and cook for 1 minute.
Reduce to medium-low, add the pearl mixture and cook for 5–7 minutes until translucent and soft through.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice and check the salt. Scatter with coriander and serve warm.

stages.title: Rinse and soak the sabudana
steps: Rinse the sabudana pearls in a sieve under cold running water for about 1 minute, until the water runs almost clear.
Tip the pearls into a bowl and add 200 ml water, just enough to level with the pearls.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 4 hours, until the pearls are soft and can be squashed easily between two fingers.
Drain in a sieve and leave for 15 minutes so the pearls are dry and separate.

stages.title: Prepare the flavourings
steps: Peel the potato and cut it into 1 cm dice.
Finely chop the green chilli and the coriander.
Coarsely crush the roasted peanuts.
Toss the drained pearls with the crushed peanuts and the salt.

stages.title: Cook the potato and spices
steps: Heat the ghee in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds, until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the potato and cook, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until golden and tender when pierced with a knife.
Stir in the green chilli and cook for 1 minute.

stages.title: Cook the sabudana
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the pearl and peanut mixture to the pan.
Cook, stirring gently, for 5–7 minutes until the pearls turn translucent and are soft all the way through.
Remove the pan from the heat.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Stir in the lime juice and taste for salt.
Scatter over the coriander and serve straight away while warm.

tips: Soak the pearls in just enough water rather than a full bowl, as excess water makes them gluey and they clump in the pan.
Rest the drained pearls for 15 minutes so surface moisture dries off, which helps them stay separate when fried.
Cook the potato until tender before adding the pearls, because the pearls need only a short time and won't soften the potato.
Add the lime juice off the heat so it stays fresh and sharp.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp white sugar with the salt for the sweet-sour balance common in Maharashtrian versions.
Replace the potato with 1 small diced sweet potato and cook it until just tender.
storage: Best eaten fresh as the pearls firm up when cold. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat in a pan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

title: Socca
summary: Thin chickpea-flour flatbread baked until blistered, with crisp edges and a peppery olive-oil finish.
method: Whisk the chickpea flour, salt, 300 ml water and 1 tbsp olive oil into a smooth batter. Rest for 30 minutes, then skim off any foam.
While it rests, heat a 28 cm cast-iron pan in the oven at 250°C (230°C fan) for at least 5 minutes, until very hot. Turn the grill on high if you have one.
Carefully remove the pan and swirl in 1 tbsp olive oil. Pour in the batter straight away to make a layer about 3 mm thick.
Bake for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the top is blistered, firm and golden in patches.
Brush with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with the black pepper. Cut into wedges and serve hot.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Sift the chickpea flour and the salt into a large bowl.
Gradually pour in 300 ml water, whisking until completely smooth with no lumps.
Whisk in 1 tbsp of the olive oil.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the bowl and leave the batter at room temperature for 30 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Skim off any foam from the surface with a spoon before cooking.

stages.title: Heat the pan
steps: While the batter rests, place a 28 cm cast-iron frying pan on the middle oven rack and heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan), or its highest setting, for at least 5 minutes until the pan is very hot.
Switch the oven grill on to high as well if your oven has one.

stages.title: Cook the socca
steps: Wearing oven mitts, carefully remove the hot pan and add 1 tbsp of the olive oil, swirling to coat the base.
Pour in the batter straight away so it forms a thin layer about 3 mm thick.
Return the pan to the oven and cook for 6–8 minutes, until the edges are crisp and the top is blistered, firm and golden in patches.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Brush the top with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle over the black pepper.
Loosen the socca with a spatula, slide it onto a board and cut into wedges.
Serve while hot and crisp at the edges.

tips: Resting the batter lets the chickpea flour absorb the water fully, giving a creamy centre instead of a gritty one.
A very hot pan sets the batter on contact, which is what creates the crisp, blistered edges.
Pour a thin layer; thick batter stays gummy in the middle before the top colours.
variations: Stir 1 tbsp chopped rosemary or thyme into the batter for a more traditional Niçoise flavour.
Top the cooked socca with crumbled feta and a handful of rocket just before serving.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 5–8 minutes until hot and crisp. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Bifana
summary: Thin pork steaks simmered in garlicky white-wine sauce and tucked into crusty bread rolls.
ingredients: 500 g pork loin, trimmed and sliced 5 mm thick
method: Pound the pork slices to about 3 mm thick between baking paper. Crush the garlic with a pinch of the salt into a paste.
Mix the garlic paste with the remaining salt, pepper, paprika, bay leaves, white wine and 1 tbsp olive oil. Add the pork, coat and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Lift out the pork, keeping the marinade, and pat dry. Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat and sear the pork in 2 batches, 1 minute per side until browned.
Pour the marinade and bay leaves into the pan and simmer over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half. Return the pork and simmer 2 minutes until cooked through with no pink remaining.
Warm the bread rolls in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 3–4 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside. Discard the bay leaves, then fill the rolls with pork and spoon over the sauce.

stages.title: Slice and pound the pork
steps: Cut the pork loin across the grain into slices about 5 mm thick, giving 8 or so slices.
Place the slices between sheets of baking paper and pound lightly with a rolling pin to an even 3 mm thickness.
Crush the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife and a pinch of the salt until pasty.

stages.title: Marinate
steps: In a non-metallic bowl, combine the garlic paste, the remaining salt, black pepper, paprika, bay leaves, white wine and 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Add the pork and turn to coat every slice.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, turning once halfway.

stages.title: Sear and simmer
steps: Lift the pork from the marinade, keeping the marinade and bay leaves, and pat the slices dry with paper towel.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat.
Sear the pork in 2 batches for 1 minute per side until browned, then set aside.
Pour the marinade and bay leaves into the pan and simmer over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half.
Return the pork and any juices to the pan and simmer for 2 minutes until cooked through with no pink remaining.

stages.title: Assemble
steps: Warm the bread rolls in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 3–4 minutes until the crust is crisp and the centre is soft.
Remove the bay leaves from the pan sauce.
Fill each roll with the pork and spoon over some sauce so it soaks into the bread.

tips: Pounding the pork thin means it cooks in minutes and stays tender instead of turning tough.
Patting the marinated pork dry before searing lets it brown rather than steam in the wine.
Dipping the cut sides of the rolls in the pan sauce is traditional and keeps the bread from tasting dry.
variations: Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the marinade for a gentle heat.
Serve with a smear of Dijon mustard in the roll, as is common in Portuguese cafes.
storage: Refrigerate the pork and sauce separately in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a pan over medium heat until steaming hot, and fill fresh rolls just before serving.

title: Baghrir
summary: Soft semolina pancakes dotted with tiny holes that soak up warm honey and melted butter.
method: Blend the semolina, flour, yeast, baking powder, salt and warm water for 2 minutes until smooth and like thin pouring cream. Pour into a jug.
Cover and rest in a warm spot for 30 minutes, until foamy and bubbly. Stir gently once.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe with a thin film of oil. Pour in about 80 ml batter and swirl into a 12 cm round.
Cook one side only for 2–3 minutes, until covered in small holes and no longer wet or shiny. Don't flip. Cool on a tea towel, holes up, and repeat for about 12.
Melt the butter and honey in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes until runny. Drizzle over the pancakes and serve.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Add the semolina, plain flour, instant yeast, baking powder and salt to a blender.
Pour in 450 ml warm water and blend for 2 minutes until completely smooth and the consistency of thin pouring cream.
Pour the batter into a large jug, scraping down the blender.

stages.title: Rest the batter
steps: Cover the jug with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm spot for 30 minutes.
The batter is ready when the surface is foamy and has risen slightly with bubbles on top.
Stir gently once; do not beat out the bubbles.

stages.title: Cook the baghrir
steps: Heat a non-stick frying pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Lightly wipe the pan with the vegetable oil on a paper towel, using only a thin film.
Pour in about 80 ml (1/3 cup) batter and swirl gently to make a round about 12 cm wide.
Cook on one side only for 2–3 minutes, until the surface is covered in small holes and no longer wet or shiny. Do not flip.
Slide the pancake onto a clean tea towel, holes facing up, and repeat with the remaining batter, wiping the pan with oil between batches only if it starts to stick. You should get about 12 pancakes.

stages.title: Make the honey butter and serve
steps: Melt the butter with the honey in a small saucepan over low heat for 2 minutes, stirring until combined and runny.
Stack the cooled pancakes in layers without pressing down, spotted side up.
Drizzle the warm honey butter over the pancakes and serve straight away.

tips: Blending for a full 2 minutes aerates the batter, which helps create the characteristic holes on the surface.
Cook on one side only; flipping closes the holes that soak up the honey butter and makes the pancake dense.
Keep the pan at medium heat: too hot and the base browns before the top sets, too cool and the bubbles fail to form.
Cool the pancakes in a single layer before stacking so the spotted tops stay dry and don't turn gluey.
variations: Swap the honey butter for a drizzle of olive oil and a spoonful of ground cinnamon-sweetened yoghurt.
Serve with warm honey and sliced almonds scattered over for crunch.
storage: Cool completely, layer with baking paper and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month. Reheat in a toaster or covered in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 5 minutes until warmed through.

title: Sesame balls
summary: Crisp golden glutinous-rice balls coated in sesame seeds with a sweet red-bean centre.
method: Dissolve the sugar in the warm water, then mix it gradually into the glutinous rice flour. Knead 2–3 minutes until smooth and soft, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Roll the red bean paste into 16 small balls of about 10 g. Divide the dough into 16 pieces of about 25 g and flatten each into a disc.
Wrap each disc around a ball of bean paste and pinch to seal. Roll smooth, moisten lightly, then coat evenly in the sesame seeds.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan over medium-low heat to 150–160°C, until a sesame seed sizzles gently without browning.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time for 6–8 minutes, turning, until puffed, floating and golden. Drain, and bring the oil back to temperature between batches.
Rest for 5 minutes, as the filling is very hot. Serve warm while the shells are crisp.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Stir the sugar into 150 ml warm water in a jug until the sugar dissolves completely.
Put the glutinous rice flour in a large bowl and pour in the sugar water a little at a time, mixing with your hand.
Knead for 2–3 minutes until the dough is smooth, soft and no longer sticks to your hands. If it cracks, knead in 1 tsp more water; if it sticks, knead in a little more flour.
Cover the bowl with a damp tea towel so the dough does not dry out.

stages.title: Fill and shape the balls
steps: Divide the red bean paste into 16 portions of about 10 g and roll each into a small ball.
Divide the dough into 16 equal pieces of about 25 g and roll each into a ball.
Flatten one dough ball into a disc about 6 cm wide, place a ball of red bean paste in the centre and fold the dough up around it.
Pinch the edges together to seal with no gaps, then roll between your palms until smooth and round.
Lightly moisten each ball with wet fingers, then roll it in the sesame seeds until evenly coated and press gently so the seeds stick.

stages.title: Fry the sesame balls
steps: Pour the oil into a deep heavy-based saucepan or wok and heat over medium-low heat to 150–160°C. A sesame seed dropped in should sizzle gently, not brown at once.
Fry 5–6 balls at a time, so the oil does not cool, for 6–8 minutes, turning gently with a slotted spoon, until the balls puff, float and are evenly golden brown.
Use the back of the spoon to press each ball very gently against the side of the pan as it fries to help it expand evenly.
Lift out with the slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack or paper towel. Return the oil to 150–160°C between batches.

stages.title: Cool and serve
steps: Rest the sesame balls for 5 minutes, as the red bean filling will be very hot inside.
Serve warm while the shells are crisp and the centres are soft and chewy.

tips: Glutinous rice flour gives the chewy texture, and regular rice flour will not work as a substitute.
Sealing the dough without gaps keeps the filling from bursting out, which would spatter hot oil.
Frying at a gentle 150–160°C lets the balls cook through and expand before the sesame seeds darken. Hotter oil browns the outside while the dough stays dense.
Roll the balls in the seeds while they are still slightly damp so the seeds stick and don't fall off in the oil.
variations: Swap the red bean paste for black sesame paste, or for a filling of 2 tbsp peanut butter mixed with 1 tbsp icing sugar.
Roll the dough balls in desiccated coconut instead of sesame seeds for a milder coating.
storage: Best eaten the day they are fried. Keep leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 8–10 minutes until hot through; they will be less crisp.

title: Frittata di zucchine
summary: A tender courgette-and-Parmesan omelette with golden edges and fresh basil.
method: Whisk the eggs with the parmesan, salt, pepper and half the torn basil. Thinly slice the zucchini into 3 mm rounds and the onion.
Heat the olive oil in a 24 cm ovenproof non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook for 8 minutes until golden at the edges and the moisture has evaporated.
Heat the grill to high. Spread the vegetables over the pan, reduce to medium-low, pour in the egg mixture and cook for 5 minutes until the edges are set and the centre is still slightly wet.
Grill for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and the centre no longer wobbles.
Rest in the pan for 3 minutes, scatter over the remaining basil and cut into 4 wedges.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and eggs
steps: Slice the zucchini into thin rounds about 3 mm thick and thinly slice the onion.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl and whisk with a fork until the yolks and whites are combined.
Stir in the parmesan, the salt, the pepper and half the torn basil leaves.
