stages.title: Cook the onion and zucchini
steps: Heat the oil in a 24 cm non-stick ovenproof frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the zucchini and cook, stirring often, for 8 minutes until golden at the edges and the moisture has evaporated from the pan.

stages.title: Set the frittata
steps: Heat the grill to high with the rack positioned about 15 cm from the element.
Spread the vegetables evenly over the base of the pan and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Pour in the egg mixture and cook for 5 minutes, without stirring, until the edges are set and the centre is still slightly wet.
Place the pan under the grill for 2–3 minutes until the top is golden and the centre is set and no longer wobbles.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the frittata in the pan for 3 minutes so it firms up for slicing.
Scatter the remaining basil over the top and cut into 4 wedges.

tips: Cooking the zucchini until the moisture has evaporated stops the frittata turning watery and helps it hold its shape when sliced.
Use a pan with an ovenproof handle, as a plastic handle will melt under the grill.
Cooking the base over low heat prevents the underside from browning too fast before the top sets.
variations: Add 100 g crumbled feta over the zucchini before pouring in the eggs for a saltier, tangier frittata.
Swap the basil for 2 tbsp chopped mint and add a pinch of chilli flakes with the onion.
storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Eat cold or reheat gently in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 10 minutes until warmed through.

title: Rote Grütze (red berry pudding)
summary: Glossy summer berries gently thickened into a ruby fruit pudding, served with cold vanilla cream.
method: Set aside about 100 g of the berries to thaw in the fridge. Whisk the cornflour with 3 tbsp cold water until smooth, and finely grate 1 tsp lemon zest.
Heat the cherry juice, caster sugar and lemon zest in a medium saucepan over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Add the remaining berries and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Reduce to medium-low, re-whisk the cornflour mixture and pour it in. Cook for 1–2 minutes until glossy and coating a spoon, then take off the heat and fold in the reserved berries.
Spoon into four glasses and cool for 30 minutes. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, until cold and softly set.
Serve cold, with the thickened cream poured over or alongside.

stages.title: Prepare the fruit and slurry
steps: Set aside a handful (about 100 g) of the berries in the fridge to fold in at the end; leave them to thaw.
Finely grate the zest from the lemons to give 1 tsp.
Whisk the cornflour with 3 tbsp cold water in a small bowl until smooth.

stages.title: Simmer the berries
steps: Combine the cherry juice, caster sugar and lemon zest in a medium saucepan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves, about 2 minutes.
Add the remaining berries and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the berries are soft and have released their juices.

stages.title: Thicken
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-low and stir the cornflour mixture again, as it settles quickly.
Pour it into the simmering fruit while stirring constantly.
Cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until the mixture turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and gently fold in the reserved berries.

stages.title: Cool and chill
steps: Spoon the grutze into four serving glasses or bowls.
Cool at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours, until cold and softly set.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Pour the thickened cream into a jug.
Serve the grutze cold, with the cream poured over or alongside.

tips: Reserving some berries and folding them in off the heat keeps a few pieces whole, so the dessert has texture as well as a smooth jelly.
Whisk the cornflour into cold water first so it doesn't form lumps when it meets the hot juice.
Boil the cornflour for a full minute or two, otherwise the grutze tastes starchy and can set loosely.
variations: Replace the cherry juice with red grape or blackcurrant juice, and reduce the sugar slightly if the juice is sweetened.
Serve with vanilla custard or cold milk instead of the cream, as is common in northern Germany.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Serve cold; the cream is best poured on just before serving. Not suitable to freeze, as it turns watery when thawed.

title: Fasolakia lathera
summary: Green beans slowly braised with tomatoes, potatoes and olive oil until meltingly tender.
ingredients: 500 g green beans, trimmed and halved
300 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
400 g tomatoes, coarsely grated, skins discarded
method: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 6–8 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the grated tomato, oregano, salt and pepper, and simmer 3–4 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the potatoes and green beans, coat in the sauce, then pour in 200 ml water and bring to a simmer.
Reduce to low, cover and cook 30–35 minutes until the beans are very soft and a knife slides easily into the potatoes.
Uncover and cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the vegetables.
Stir through the parsley, adjust the salt, and serve warm or at room temperature.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Trim the stalk ends from the green beans and cut them in half.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 3 cm chunks.
Cut the tomatoes in half and grate the cut sides on a box grater into a bowl, discarding the skins.
Thinly slice the onion and garlic, and finely chop the parsley.

stages.title: Build the sauce base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 6–8 minutes until soft and translucent but not browned.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the grated tomato, then add the oregano, salt and black pepper, and simmer for 3–4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.

stages.title: Braise the beans and potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes and green beans to the pot and stir to coat in the sauce.
Pour in 200 ml water and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 30–35 minutes, stirring gently every 10 minutes, until the beans are very soft and a knife slides easily into the potatoes.

stages.title: Reduce and finish
steps: Remove the lid and cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the vegetables.
Stir through the parsley, taste and add more salt if needed, then serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Grating the tomatoes gives a smooth sauce without tough skins, so the dish stays silky after a long braise.
Greek beans are cooked until very soft rather than crisp; the long, gentle braise lets them absorb the oil and tomato.
The generous olive oil is what makes this dish 'lathera' (oily) and gives the sauce its body, so don't cut it back too far.
Cutting the potatoes into chunks of similar size means they finish cooking at the same time as the beans.
variations: Serve with crumbled feta and crusty bread to mop up the sauce.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the oregano for a gentle heat.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat until hot, adding a splash of water if the sauce has thickened. It is also good served cold.

title: Bánh xèo
summary: Crisp turmeric rice crêpes filled with prawns, pork and bean sprouts, wrapped in fresh herbs.
ingredients: 150 g pork loin, thinly sliced into strips
method: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric, salt, coconut milk, 250 ml water and spring onions into a smooth batter. Rest 20 minutes, thinning with a little water if thick.
Stir the lime juice from 2 limes, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and 60 ml water until the sugar dissolves. Cut the last lime into wedges.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the pork and garlic 3–4 minutes until cooked through, then the prawns 2–3 minutes until pink. Season with pepper and set aside.
Heat a little oil in the pan over medium-high. Pour in 125 ml batter, top with a quarter of the pork, prawns and bean sprouts, cover and cook 2 minutes.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook over medium heat 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Fold, then repeat for 4 pancakes, keeping them warm in a 100°C oven.
Serve the pancakes torn up and wrapped in lettuce with the mint, coriander and lime wedges, dipped in the sauce.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the rice flour, turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt in a large bowl.
Whisk in the coconut milk and 250 ml water until smooth, then stir in the spring onions.
Rest the batter for 20 minutes so the flour hydrates; it should be the consistency of thin pouring cream, so whisk in a little more water if thick.

stages.title: Make the dipping sauce
steps: Juice 2 of the limes (about 80 ml) and cut the remaining lime into wedges.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and 60 ml water until the sugar dissolves, then set aside.

stages.title: Cook the pork and prawns
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat.
Cook the pork and garlic for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until browned and cooked through with no pink remaining.
Add the prawns and cook for 2–3 minutes until pink and opaque, then season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Transfer to a plate and wipe the pan clean.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat 1 tsp of the remaining oil in the same pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Stir the batter, then pour in about 125 ml, swirling to coat the base thinly; it should sizzle immediately.
Scatter a quarter of the pork and prawns and a small handful of bean sprouts over one half, then cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Uncover, drizzle 1 tsp oil around the edge, and cook over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the underside is deep golden and the edges are crisp.
Fold the pancake in half, slide onto a plate, and repeat to make 4 pancakes, keeping them warm in a 100°C (80°C fan) oven.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Arrange the lettuce, mint, coriander and lime wedges on a platter.
Serve the pancakes hot, torn into pieces, wrapped in lettuce with the herbs and dipped in the sauce.

tips: Resting the batter lets the rice flour absorb the liquid, giving a crisper, more tender pancake that doesn't tear.
Get the pan properly hot before pouring; the sizzle sets the base quickly and creates the lacy crisp edge.
Slice the pork thinly so it cooks through in minutes and doesn't turn tough.
variations: Replace the pork and prawns with sliced mushrooms and cubed firm tofu, and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce in the dip for a vegetarian version.
Add thin slices of cooked chicken thigh instead of pork.
storage: Store cooked pancakes and fillings separately in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat pancakes in a hot dry pan for 1–2 minutes per side until crisp and heated through; the batter keeps 2 days in the fridge.

title: Devilled eggs
summary: Creamy mustard-and-mayo yolk filling piped into tender egg whites with a dusting of paprika.
method: Lower the eggs into boiling water in a saucepan over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 10 minutes, until the yolks are cooked through and pale yellow.
Chill the eggs in ice water for 15 minutes, until completely cold. Peel under cold running water and pat dry.
Halve the eggs lengthways. Mash the yolks until fine and crumbly, then stir in the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Spoon or pipe the filling into the whites. Refrigerate for 10 minutes to firm up.
Dust with the paprika, scatter over the chives and serve.

stages.title: Boil the eggs
steps: Lower the eggs gently into a saucepan of boiling water over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium so the water simmers steadily.
Cook for 10 minutes, until the whites are firm and the yolks are cooked through and pale yellow.
Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with cold water and plenty of ice.

stages.title: Cool and peel
steps: Lift the eggs into the ice water with a slotted spoon and leave for 15 minutes, until completely cold.
Tap each egg all over on the bench, then peel under cold running water so the shell slips off without tearing the whites.
Pat the eggs dry with paper towel.

stages.title: Make the filling
steps: Cut each egg in half lengthways and pop the yolks into a bowl, keeping the whites intact.
Mash the yolks with a fork until fine and crumbly.
Add the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, white vinegar, salt and black pepper and stir until smooth and creamy.
Taste and add a little more salt if needed.

stages.title: Fill and chill
steps: Spoon the filling into the egg whites, or pipe it using a piping bag with a star nozzle for a neater finish.
Refrigerate the eggs, uncovered or loosely covered, for 10 minutes to firm up.
Dust with the paprika, scatter over the chives and serve.

tips: Cooling the eggs in ice water stops the cooking, which prevents a grey-green ring around the yolks and makes the shells easier to peel.
Eggs that are a week or two old peel more cleanly than very fresh ones, so you lose less white.
Mash the yolks to a fine crumb before adding the wet ingredients, because lumps will not smooth out once the mayonnaise goes in.
Wiping the bench and trimming a thin slice off the base of each white stops the eggs sliding around on the platter.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp finely chopped crispy bacon into the filling for a smoky, salty version.
Replace the paprika topping with a pinch of cayenne pepper and a few pickled jalapeno slices for heat.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Serve cold and do not reheat.

title: Bhindi masala
summary: Tender okra stir-fried with onions, tomatoes and aromatic spices until lightly crisp and savoury.
method: Dry the okra well, trim and slice into 2 cm pieces. Finely chop the onion and garlic, and chop the tomatoes.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the okra in batches for 8–10 minutes until browned and tender, then set aside.
Heat the remaining oil over medium heat and cook the onion for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 8–10 minutes until a thick paste and the oil separates.
Return the okra and cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until coated and heated through.
Stir through the garam masala and half the coriander leaves, then serve topped with the rest.

stages.title: Prepare the okra and aromatics
steps: Wash the okra, then dry each pod thoroughly with a clean tea towel so it doesn't turn slimy when cooked.
Trim the tops and tails, then slice the okra into 2 cm pieces.
Finely chop the onion and garlic, and chop the tomatoes.

stages.title: Brown the okra
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat.

Add the okra in a single layer, working in two batches if the pan is crowded, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8–10 minutes until the edges are browned and the pieces are tender when pierced with a knife.
Transfer the okra to a plate and wipe out the pan.

stages.title: Make the masala
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt, then cook, stirring and pressing the tomatoes down, for 8–10 minutes until broken down into a thick paste and the oil begins to separate at the edges.

stages.title: Combine and finish
steps: Return the okra to the pan and fold it gently through the masala.
Cook over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until the okra is coated and heated through.
Sprinkle over the garam masala and half the chopped coriander, then toss once.
Serve scattered with the remaining coriander.

tips: Drying the okra fully before cutting limits the sticky mucilage that makes it slimy.
Browning the okra separately over high heat sears the cut surfaces, which keeps the pieces from turning mushy in the masala.
Cooking the tomatoes until the oil separates removes their raw sharpness and gives a concentrated masala.
Adding the garam masala at the end keeps its aroma, which fades with long cooking.
variations: Add 1 tsp amchur or a squeeze of lemon juice at the end for a tangy dry-style bhindi.
Stir in 1 diced potato, cooked in the pan with the onion, to make it more filling.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat until steaming hot throughout.

title: Tarte flambée
summary: A paper-thin Alsatian flatbread topped with crème fraîche, onions and smoky bacon.
ingredients: 150 g bacon, cut into thin strips
method: Mix the flour, salt, water and olive oil into a dough, then knead for 3–4 minutes until smooth and elastic. Divide into 2 balls and cover.
Stir the nutmeg and pepper into the crème fraîche. Slice the onion very thinly and cut the bacon into 1 cm strips.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) with 2 large trays inside. Rest the dough for 20 minutes.
Roll each ball on baking paper into a very thin oval, 2–3 mm thick. Spread with the crème fraîche mixture, leaving a 1 cm border, and top with the onion and bacon.
Slide onto the hot trays and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are browned, the bacon is cooked and the onion is lightly charred.
Rest for 2 minutes, then cut and serve hot.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl and make a well in the centre.
Pour in 125 ml water and the olive oil, then mix with a spoon until a rough dough forms.
Knead on a lightly floured bench for 3–4 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 2 equal pieces, shape into balls and cover with a clean tea towel.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Stir the nutmeg and a generous grind of black pepper into the crème fraîche.
Slice the onion as thinly as you can and separate the slices into rings.
Cut the bacon into thin strips about 1 cm wide.

stages.title: Rest the dough and heat the oven
steps: Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan) and put 2 large baking trays on separate shelves to heat up.
Leave the dough covered to rest for 20 minutes so it rolls out thinly without springing back.

stages.title: Shape and top the tartes
steps: Roll each dough ball on a sheet of baking paper into a very thin oval or rectangle, about 2–3 mm thick.
Spread half the crème fraîche mixture over each base, leaving a 1 cm border.
Scatter the onion and bacon evenly over both bases.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Carefully slide each tarte on its baking paper onto a hot tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the edges are crisp and browned, the bacon is cooked and browned at the tips, and the onion is softened and lightly charred.
Swap the trays between shelves after 6 minutes if one side is browning faster.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the tartes on a board for 2 minutes so the base firms up.
Cut each into pieces with a sharp knife or pizza wheel and serve hot.

tips: Roll the dough very thin, because a thick base turns bready instead of crisp like a traditional tarte flambée.
Preheating the trays gives the base an immediate blast of heat from underneath, which crisps the underside before the topping releases moisture.
Slice the onion paper-thin so it softens and chars in the short bake instead of staying raw and sharp.
Leave a border when spreading the crème fraîche so it doesn't run off the edge and burn on the tray.
variations: Add 100 g grated gruyere over the crème fraîche for a richer, gratinée-style tarte.
For a sweet version, omit the bacon and onion, top with thinly sliced apples and a sprinkle of caster sugar and cinnamon, and bake until the apple edges are golden.
storage: Best eaten straight away while crisp. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days and reheat on a tray in a 200°C (180°C fan) oven for 5–6 minutes until hot through and crisp.

title: Ricotta gnocchi
summary: Pillowy ricotta dumplings tossed in brown butter and sage for a delicate, comforting pasta dish.
method: Drain the ricotta in a towel-lined sieve in the fridge for 25 minutes, until noticeably drier and crumbly.
Mix the ricotta with the egg, parmesan, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper until smooth. Gently fold in 100 g of the flour until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Roll the dough into 2 cm ropes on a bench dusted with the remaining flour, cut into 2–3 cm pieces and chill on a floured tray for 10 minutes.
Bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat with the remaining 3 tsp salt, then reduce to a simmer. Cook the dumplings in 2 batches for 2–3 minutes, until they float and are cooked through.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until foaming. Add the sage and cook for 1–2 minutes, until nutty, golden-brown and crisp.
Toss the dumplings through the sage butter for 1 minute, until coated and lightly golden. Serve straight away.

stages.title: Drain the ricotta
steps: Line a sieve with a clean tea towel or paper towels and sit it over a bowl.
Tip in the ricotta, then cover and leave to drain in the fridge for 25 minutes, until noticeably drier and crumbly.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Tip the drained ricotta into a large bowl and add the egg, the parmesan, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Stir with a fork until smooth, then add 100 g of the flour.
Fold gently just until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms, as overmixing makes the dumplings tough.

stages.title: Shape the dumplings
steps: Dust a bench and a tray generously with some of the remaining 40 g flour.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces and roll each into a rope about 2 cm thick, dusting lightly as needed.
Cut each rope into 2–3 cm pieces and place them on the floured tray in a single layer.

stages.title: Chill and heat the water
steps: Refrigerate the tray, uncovered, for 10 minutes so the dumplings firm up and hold their shape in the water.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat and add the remaining 3 tsp salt.

stages.title: Cook the dumplings
steps: Reduce the water to a gentle simmer.
Cook the dumplings in 2 batches for 2–3 minutes each, until they float to the surface and are firm and cooked through when one is cut open.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon onto a plate, keeping them in a single layer.

stages.title: Brown the sage butter
steps: Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until foaming, about 1 minute.
Add the sage leaves and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the butter smells nutty and turns golden-brown and the leaves are crisp.
Add the cooked dumplings and toss gently for 1 minute, until coated and lightly golden. Serve straight away.

tips: Draining the ricotta removes excess moisture, so you need less flour and the dumplings stay light rather than rubbery.
Cook one test piece first. If it falls apart, mix in another tablespoon of flour before shaping the rest.
Chilling the shaped dough helps it set, so the pieces are less likely to break up in the simmering water.
Keep the water at a gentle simmer, as a rolling boil can break up these soft dumplings.
variations: Stir 100 g blanched, squeezed-dry and finely chopped baby spinach into the dough for a spinach and ricotta version.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes and the finely grated zest of 1 lemon to the browned butter for a sharper finish.
storage: Refrigerate cooked gnocchi in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat with a little butter until hot through. Uncooked shaped gnocchi can be frozen on a tray, then bagged, and cooked from frozen for 3–4 minutes.

title: Carciofi alla romana
summary: Tender artichokes braised in olive oil, garlic, mint and lemon in the Roman style.
method: Squeeze one lemon into a large bowl of cold water. Snap the tough outer leaves off the artichokes until pale yellow-green, cut off the top third and peel the stems.
Rub all cut surfaces with the other lemon half, scoop out the fuzzy chokes and keep the artichokes in the lemon water.
Mix the garlic, parsley, mint, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp olive oil. Drain the artichokes and spoon the mixture into the centres and between the outer leaves.

Stand the artichokes stem-up in a snug saucepan with the water and remaining 2 tbsp olive oil. Simmer over medium heat, cover, then cook on low for 30–35 minutes, until a knife slips easily into the stems.
Uncover and simmer over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, until the juices turn glossy. Rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm with the juices and a squeeze of lemon.

stages.title: Trim the artichokes
steps: Halve 1 lemon and squeeze the juice of the second lemon into a large bowl of cold water (about 1 litre); keep the squeezed halves in the bowl.
Snap off the tough outer leaves of each artichoke until you reach pale yellow-green leaves, then cut off the top third of the remaining leaves.
Peel the stems and trim the base, then rub all cut surfaces with the cut lemon half.
Spread the leaves open slightly with your thumbs, scoop out the fuzzy choke with a teaspoon, and drop each artichoke into the lemon water.

stages.title: Season the artichokes
steps: Mix the garlic, parsley, mint, salt and a few grinds of black pepper with 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a small bowl.
Drain the artichokes and shake out the excess water.
Spoon the herb mixture into the centres and press some between the outer leaves.

stages.title: Braise the artichokes
steps: Choose a saucepan just wide enough to hold the artichokes snugly, and stand them stem-up in it.
Pour in the 200 ml water and the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cover and reduce to low heat.
Cook for 30–35 minutes, until the stems and bases slip off a knife tip easily and an outer leaf pulls away with no resistance.
If the liquid evaporates before the artichokes are tender, add 50 ml water.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Remove the lid and simmer over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, until the liquid reduces to a glossy sauce.
Rest the artichokes in the pan juices for 5 minutes, then serve warm with the juices spooned over and a squeeze of the lemon.

tips: Rubbing cut surfaces with lemon straight away stops the flesh oxidising and turning brown and bitter.
Standing the artichokes stem-up in a snug pan keeps them upright so they steam in the oil and water and the herbs stay in the centres.
Peeling the stems lets you eat them; the inner stem is as tender and sweet as the heart.
variations: Add 1 tsp chilli flakes to the herb mixture for a gentle heat.
Replace the mint with 1 tbsp chopped fresh thyme for a more earthy flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container with the cooking juices for up to 2 days. Serve at room temperature or reheat gently in a covered pan over low heat until warmed through.

title: Île flottante
summary: Cloudlike poached meringues floating on chilled vanilla custard with ribbons of amber caramel.
method: Separate the eggs, yolks in one bowl and whites in another. Heat the milk with the vanilla over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming, then take off the heat.
Whisk the yolks with 50 g of the sugar until pale, then whisk in the warm milk. Cook in the pan over low heat for 6–8 minutes until it coats a spoon. Strain.
Cover the custard surface with baking paper and refrigerate for at least 2 hours until completely cold.
Beat the whites with the salt until foamy, then add 30 g of the sugar and beat until stiff and glossy. Simmer the water in a frying pan over medium-low heat.
Poach 4 large spoonfuls of meringue for 1 minute each side until puffed and firm. Drain. Melt the remaining 40 g sugar in a pan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until amber.
Pour the cold custard into 4 bowls, float a meringue on each and drizzle with the caramel.

stages.title: Separate the eggs and warm the milk
steps: Separate the 4 eggs, putting the yolks in a medium heatproof bowl and the whites in a large, clean, dry bowl.
Pour the milk into a medium saucepan and add the vanilla extract.
Heat the milk over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge, then remove from the heat.

stages.title: Make the custard
steps: Whisk the yolks with 50 g of the caster sugar for 1–2 minutes until pale and thick.
Slowly pour the warm milk into the yolks, whisking constantly, then return the mixture to the saucepan.

Stir with a wooden spoon over low heat for 6–8 minutes until the custard thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon and a finger drawn through it leaves a clear line. Do not let it boil or it will scramble.
Strain the custard through a fine sieve into a jug or shallow serving dish.

stages.title: Chill the custard
steps: Press baking paper onto the surface of the custard to stop a skin forming.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until completely cold.

stages.title: Poach the meringues
steps: Whisk the egg whites with the pinch of salt using electric beaters on medium speed for 1–2 minutes until foamy.
Add 30 g of the caster sugar a spoonful at a time, then beat on high for 2–3 minutes until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Bring the 1 litre water to a bare simmer in a wide frying pan over medium-low heat, with only tiny bubbles breaking the surface.
Using two spoons, shape the meringue into 4 large ovals and slip them into the water. Poach for 1 minute on each side until puffed and firm to the touch.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towel.

stages.title: Make the caramel and serve
steps: Put the remaining 40 g caster sugar in a small, clean saucepan over medium heat. Do not stir; swirl the pan occasionally for 4–5 minutes until the sugar melts into a golden amber caramel.
Remove from the heat as soon as it is amber, as it darkens quickly and turns bitter.
Pour the cold custard into 4 shallow bowls and float a meringue on each.
Drizzle the caramel over the meringues and serve straight away.

tips: Stirring the custard over low heat and straining it protects the yolks from curdling and catches any small lumps.
Poaching below a simmer keeps the meringues tender; fast bubbling makes them rubbery and they collapse.
A clean, dry bowl with no trace of yolk lets the whites whip to stiff peaks.
Add the caramel just before serving, as it softens and melts into the meringue if left to stand.
variations: Use a split vanilla pod instead of extract: scrape the seeds into the milk, add the pod, and remove it before making the custard.
Scatter toasted flaked almonds over the top for crunch.
storage: Keep the custard and meringues separate, covered in the fridge, for up to 2 days. Add the meringues and fresh caramel just before serving. Do not freeze.

title: Shish barak
summary: Tiny lamb-filled dumplings gently simmered in warm garlicky yoghurt sauce with dried mint.
method: Mix the flour, half the salt and 130 ml water into a dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic, then rest under a damp tea towel for 25 minutes.
Cook the onion in 1 tbsp of the oil in a pan over medium heat for 4 minutes. Add the lamb, cinnamon, remaining salt and pepper, and cook over medium-high until browned and no pink remains. Cool.
Roll the dough 2 mm thick and cut 6 cm circles. Fill each with 1 tsp of the filling, fold and seal, then pinch the corners together.
Toss the dumplings with the remaining oil and bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 15–18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

Whisk the yoghurt, egg and cornflour in a saucepan, adding water if thick. Heat over medium until simmering, then simmer on low for 10 minutes until thickened. Add the dumplings and simmer for 5 minutes until tender.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and fry the garlic for 1 minute until golden. Stir in the mint for 10 seconds, then spoon over the dumplings and serve.

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl, then add 130 ml water and mix to a shaggy dough.
Knead on a bench for 5 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover with a damp tea towel and rest for 25 minutes.

stages.title: Cook the lamb filling
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the lamb mince, cinnamon, the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper, breaking up the mince with a spoon.
Cook for 6–8 minutes over medium-high heat until browned, cooked through with no pink remaining, and dry.
Tip onto a plate and cool for 10 minutes.

stages.title: Shape the dumplings
steps: Roll the dough out on a floured bench until 2 mm thick and cut into 6 cm circles.
Place 1 tsp of the filling in the centre of each circle, fold over into a half moon and press the edges firmly to seal.
Bring the two corners together, pinch to join and set on a floured tray.

stages.title: Bake the dumplings
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Toss the dumplings with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil on the tray in a single layer.
Bake for 15–18 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.

stages.title: Cook the yoghurt sauce
steps: Whisk the yoghurt, egg and cornflour in a large saucepan until smooth, then add 250 ml cold water if the mixture feels very thick.
Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction, until it comes to a gentle simmer, about 10 minutes.
Reduce to low and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened and the egg is cooked through.
Add the baked dumplings and simmer for 5 minutes over low heat until the pastry is tender.

stages.title: Fry the garlic and mint
steps: Melt the butter in a small frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the garlic for 1 minute until fragrant and just golden, then stir in the dried mint for 10 seconds.
Spoon the garlic and mint over the dumplings in the sauce and serve hot.

tips: Stirring the yoghurt in one direction and bringing it up slowly keeps the egg and cornflour stabilising it, so it does not split.
Dry the lamb filling well, because excess moisture makes the dumplings soggy and hard to seal.
Rolling the dough very thin gives tender dumplings; thick dough stays chewy after simmering.
Greek yoghurt is thick enough to give a creamy sauce without long reduction.
variations: Swap the lamb for beef mince and add 1/2 tsp ground allspice to the filling.
Serve over cooked rice to stretch the dish further.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water, stirring, and do not boil.

title: Lablabi
summary: Warm chickpeas in a cumin-garlic broth poured over torn bread, finished with lemon and harissa.
ingredients: 4 thick slices crusty bread, torn into bite-sized pieces
method: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Crush the garlic, juice the lemon, and tear the bread into bite-sized pieces into 4 deep bowls.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, ground cumin and cumin seeds for 30–60 seconds until fragrant, then stir in 1 tbsp harissa for 30 seconds.
Add the chickpeas, stock and salt, and bring to the boil over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes until the chickpeas are very tender.
Crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the pan to thicken the broth. Stir in the lemon juice, simmer for 2 minutes, and season to taste.
Ladle the chickpeas and broth over the bread in the bowls. Top with the remaining harissa and serve straight away.

stages.title: Prepare the chickpeas and bread
steps: Drain the chickpeas into a colander and rinse under cold water, then set aside.
Crush the garlic and juice the lemon.
Tear the bread into bite-sized pieces and divide among 4 deep bowls.

stages.title: Build the flavour base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the garlic, ground cumin and cumin seeds and stir for 30–60 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Stir in 1 tbsp of the harissa and cook for 30 seconds.

stages.title: Simmer the broth
steps: Add the chickpeas, vegetable stock and salt, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes, until the chickpeas are very tender.
Crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pan with a wooden spoon to thicken the broth.
Stir in the lemon juice and simmer for 2 minutes. Taste and add more salt if needed.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Ladle the hot chickpeas and broth over the bread so it soaks up the liquid.
Top each bowl with a little of the remaining harissa, and serve straight away.

tips: Rinsing canned chickpeas removes the starchy canning liquid, which can make the broth taste flat.
Crushing some of the chickpeas thickens the broth without flour or cream, giving the traditional soupy but hearty texture.
Use stale or day-old bread if you can, because it soaks up the broth without turning to mush.
Add harissa at the table as well as in the pot, as brands vary a lot in heat.
variations: Top each bowl with a soft-boiled or poached egg, cooked until the white is set and the yolk is runny, or cooked through if you prefer.
Add a drained can of tuna and a spoonful of capers on top of each bowl for a more traditional street-style version.
storage: Store the broth without the bread in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot, then pour over fresh bread.

title: Lohikeitto
summary: Tender salmon, potatoes and leeks in a delicate creamy dill broth with a fresh lemon finish.
ingredients: 500 g salmon fillet, skin removed, pin-boned
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
2 leeks, white and pale green parts only, halved and sliced
method: Cut the salmon into 3 cm cubes and chill. Cube the potatoes, dice the carrot, slice the leeks and rinse them well, and chop the dill.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the leeks and carrot with the salt for 6–7 minutes, until the leeks are soft and glossy but not browned.
Add the potatoes, chicken stock and 200 ml water. Boil over high heat, then simmer on medium-low for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into a potato.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the salmon and cream and cook for 4–5 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily. Don't let it boil.
Off the heat, stir in the dill, lemon juice and pepper. Season with more salt or lemon if needed and serve in warm bowls.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and salmon
steps: Cut the salmon into 3 cm cubes and refrigerate until needed.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes, then dice the carrot into 1 cm pieces.
Halve the leeks lengthways, slice them and rinse well in a colander to remove grit, then drain.
Pick the dill fronds from the stalks and chop them roughly.

stages.title: Soften the leeks and carrot
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the leeks and carrot and the salt, and cook, stirring often, for 6–7 minutes until the leeks are soft and glossy but not browned.

stages.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps: Add the potatoes and pour in the chicken stock and 200 ml water.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into a potato cube.

stages.title: Poach the salmon
steps: Reduce the heat to low so the soup barely bubbles.
Add the salmon cubes and the cream and cook for 4–5 minutes, until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
Do not let the soup boil once the cream is in, or it may split.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the chopped dill, lemon juice and black pepper.
Taste and add a little more salt or lemon juice if needed, then ladle into warm bowls.

tips: Waxy potatoes hold their shape in the soup, while floury ones break down and make it cloudy and thick.
Add the salmon last and keep the heat low, as it cooks in a few minutes and turns dry and chalky if boiled.
Add the lemon juice off the heat so the cream does not curdle and the dill stays fresh.
Rinse the sliced leeks well, because grit collects between the layers and ruins the soup.
variations: Replace half the salmon with firm white fish fillets, cut into the same size cubes, for a milder soup.
Add 1 tsp ground allspice berries or a few whole allspice berries with the stock for a more traditional Finnish flavour.
storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat without boiling. Not suitable for freezing because the cream and potatoes change texture.
